Additive manufacturing compression overmolding process: (a) Laser powder bed fusion of triangular maraging steel lattice structure with an overall size of 152.4 mm x 152.4 mm, (b) Big area additive manufacturing (BAAM) of carbon fiber reinforced polyamide-6,6 (40% wt. CF/PA66), and (c) Compression overmolding of polymer composite on top of metal lattice to create hybrid structure. The above-mentioned AM-CM process was repeated with metal inserts of two different thicknesses of 4 mm and 13 mm. The flowability of the polymer composite into the metal lattice is investigated on these two different thickness metal lattices. The manufactured hybrid panel of 4 mm thick is shown in Fig. 3.3.2(a). The cross-sectional and microscopic images in Fig. 3.3.2(a) illustrate good flowability of 40% wt. 6 | P age CF/PA66 composite into the metal mesh and creating mechanical interlocks between dissimilar materials without a bonding agent. In case of 13 mm thick panel, the polymer composite did not penetrate through the thickness of the metal mesh as shown in Fig. 3.3.2(b). Because the 40% wt. CF/PA66 did not penetrate the 13 mm thick panel, only 4 mm hybrid panels manufactured in the small molds were considered further Coupon specimens were extracted from these panels in both the deposition direction (aligned with the path of the printing head) and in orthogonal direction (perpendicular to the deposition direction) for tensile testing (refer Section 5.3). CF/PA66) into maraging steel mesh of (a) 4 mm, and (b) 13 mm thick. 3.3.2 Overmolding in large (14” x 14”) mold The metal inserts were designed through an iterative process to enable between mechanical bonding between the metal and polymer composite without the use of any adhesives or bonding agents. To test these designs, metallic specimens were fabricated using binder jetting and overmolded as described here. The tensile and shear specimens fabricated through binder jetting process are shown in Fig. 3.3.3(a). The CF/PA66 LFT preform was fabricated using BAAM and machined to 14” x 14” to exactly fit within the mold (refer Fig.3.3.3(b)). Next, the tensile specimens are placed within the mold as shown in Fig. 3.3.3(c). The AM preform was preheated in Protherm oven. The Protherm oven was first heated up to 3710 C and the AM preform was placed inside the oven for 7 minutes. Next, the preform was flipped on the other side and heated in the oven for another 7 minutes before moving it to the mold to be placed on top of the metal specimens. The preheated AM preform before placing it in the mold is shown in Fig. 3.3.3(c). Once the AM preform was placed in the mold, the compression process was initiated to exert a 50 ton-force for 7 | P age 1 min.
